paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this passage. Jeremiah doesn't dress it up. He tells the LORD his pain is unending, his wound is incurable, and God feels like "a mirage" to him (Jeremiah 15:18). And the LORD doesn't scold him for saying it. He answers him. You can bring God your honest, messy, loud-in-the-kitchen feelings, and He still talks back.

Now look at HOW the LORD answers. He says, "If you return, I will restore you; you will stand in My presence" (Jeremiah 15:19). He also tells Jeremiah that the people must turn to him, but he must not turn to them. I think that's the heart of it: when the crowd is loud, you don't change the message to fit the crowd. You stay close to God and keep speaking what is noble, not worthless.

And then comes the promise I would frame and hang over my ovens. The LORD says He will make Jeremiah a fortified wall of bronze, and though they will fight against him, they "will not overcome" him, "for I am with you to save and deliver you" (Jeremiah 15:20). Notice it doesn't say the fighting stops. It says God is WITH him in it. So baker, when you're the one sitting alone while the party roars down the hall, remember Jeremiah's joy came from God's words (Jeremiah 15:16), and God's presence is the wall around you.
